title: Fragmented ledger constructor for per-route cost & latency profiles
creator: Marco Alvarez
description:
Summary:
We need a backend component that assembles per-route, per-model, and per-customer cost+latency ledgers from fragmented telemetry sources (runtime traces, batching logs, token counts, kernel-level metrics). The goal is a deterministic ledger builder that produces time-windowed profiles (1m, 1h, 24h) used by Console dashboards, chargeback APIs, and alerting rules.

Problem statement:
Current pipelines produce loosely correlated metrics (separate token tallies, latency histograms, and model-run records) that are expensive to join downstream and result in inconsistent per-route chargebacks. This ticket implements a service to canonicalize and join the fragments into a compact ledger that is:
- deterministically aggregatable across shards
- tolerant of delayed/duplicate events
- performant for both streaming and backfill workloads

Goals & acceptance criteria:
1) Produce per-route/model/customer ledger entries containing: route_id, model_id, customer_id, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_input, tokens_generated, total_compute_ms, p50/p95 latency_ms, batch_count, kernel_gpu_ms, derived_cost_usd.
2) End-to-end latency for streaming updates under steady-state: <= 30s for 95th percentile.
3) Backfill throughput: support 200k fragments/minute without impacting production consumers.
4) Deterministic idempotent writes so repeated ingestion does not double-count.
5) Output schema and access APIs documented and consumed by Console chargeback endpoint and billing ingestion job.

Design sketch:
- Input: three primary fragment streams (trace-events, token-logs, runtime-metrics). Each fragment includes a canonical fragment_id and causal_span_id.
- Join strategy: use causal_span_id as a soft join key; fall back to time-window heuristics for missing spans.
- Construction: accumulate fragments in a windowed state store keyed by (route_id, model_id, customer_id, window_start). When window closes (T=window_end+grace_period) compute ledger row and write to ledger topic.
- Storage: compacted Kafka ledger topic for downstream consumers + periodic materialized views in OLAP (BigQuery/ClickHouse) for fast Console queries.
- Exactly-once strategy: use fragment_id deduplication with a Bloom filter + local LRU for hot keys and rely on write-once ledger topic semantics to avoid duplication.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong consistency vs low latency: chosen design favors eventual consistency with short reconciliation runs to maintain low latency for dashboards.
- Stateful streaming vs micro-batch: streaming chosen to meet 30s SLA; micro-batch reserved for large historical backfills.
- Dedup memory footprint vs accuracy: Bloom filter with probabilistic false positives chosen to limit memory; reconciler job corrects rare false positives on nightly runs.

Open questions / risk:
- How to attribute kernel_gpu_ms when a single kernel run serves multiple routes (shared batching)? Proposed heuristic: apportion GPU time by token_share within batch; capture per-request batch_token_count at runtime. Accuracy vs overhead tradeoff needs validation.
- Cost USD model: which price curve do we use for mixed instance types? Coordination with billing team required.

Deliverables:
- Streaming service (Go) that consumes fragments, builds ledger rows, and writes to ledger topic.
- Reconciliation backfill job and verification harness.
- Contract docs for Console and billing consumers (schema + retention).
- Benchmarks: latency, throughput, and memory usage under synthetic workloads.

Acceptance tests:
- Integration test with synthetic tracer producing out-of-order fragments; ledger rows should match expected aggregates.
- Nightly job validates ledger totals vs raw token tallies within 0.5% for a 24h window.

Notes on data retention & privacy:
- Ledger entries will include customer_id but no raw prompts. Retain ledgers for 90 days in low-latency store and longer in cold storage per compliance.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Spike: assemble sample fragments and validate join heuristics (2d).
2) Prototype streaming join + write to a test ledger topic (5d).
3) Add dedup + idempotent write semantics (3d).
4) Performance tuning + resource sizing + runbook (4d).
5) Integration with Console and billing (2d).

Related artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Fragmented+Ledger+Constructor (work-in-progress)
- Spike notebook & synthetic generator: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/rdw-fragment-spike
comments: 2026-03-09 - Marco Alvarez: Kickoff spike complete. Generated synthetic fragments for three routes and validated causal_span_id as a high-signal join key. Observed 92% match rate when span present, falling to 68% when relying on time-window heuristics. Uploaded sample datasets to Drive.

2026-03-10 - Rina Patel: Benchmarked local prototype consumer (single-threaded) ingesting 50k fragments/min with ~18s 95th latency. Memory peaked at 2.1GB per shard. Need multi-threading and batching to meet 200k/min target. Filed a concurrency follow-up (ENG-612380).

2026-03-10 - Dev Review (A. Chen): Reviewed design doc. Recommended clarifying the dedup window and grace_period sizing. Concern: Bloom filter false positive rate calculation missing. Action: add math & CI thresholds in doc.

2026-03-11 - Rina Patel: Implemented initial dedup with cuckoo filter library. False-positive tests show ~0.08% at 1e6 keys. Added unit tests and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3198

2026-03-11 - Finance (S. Gupta): Confirmed we should use reserved-cost curves for Dedicated GPU attribution and on-demand curves for Hosted. Shared pricing table: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/pricing-model

2026-03-12 - Ops (E. Nakamura): Noted replication factor and topic retention settings for the ledger topic. Suggested compacted topic + separate retention for recent N days to keep OLAP costs manageable. Open action: define exact retention numbers (ENG-612381).

2026-03-12 - Rina Patel: Pushed prototype service branch to feature/ledger-constructor. Running canary consumer in staging, linking dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ledger-proto. Observed p95 end-to-end 22s under synthetic load (50k/min). Next: parallelize shards and finalize apportionment heuristic.
2026-03-12 - Marco Alvarez: Added acceptance test plan to Confluence and created a validation harness that compares ledger outputs to ground truth. Harness located at drive path in design doc.
